We are proposing to correct an error in the name of one specialization in the Master of Environmental Science and Management (MESM) program so that it accurately reflects program offerings and requirements. There is currently a discrepancy between the MESM specializations approved by Faculty Senate Bill 16-17-10B (and, therefore, available in ecampus) and the specializations described in the graduate catalog and the MESM website. Both the graduate catalog and the MESM website currently include a specialization in “Environmental Policy and Management”, while ecampus instead has a specialization called “Environmental Science and Management.”

From the inception of MESM many years ago, Environmental Policy and Management has been one of the core tracks, and many students have chosen this specialization specifically because of its emphasis on integrating social science and policy with natural science expertise. Unfortunately, under the current ecampus settings, their transcripts describe the specialization as “Environmental Science and Management” rather than “Environment Policy and Management.” This language does not accurately reflect the knowledge and skills they gain in that specialization. We would therefore like to correct the approved name of the specialization to match what we are currently advertising and providing students. Specifically, we are proposing to change the “Environmental Science and Management” specialization (Academic Plan: MESMESM) to the “Environmental Policy and Management” specialization (Academic Plan: MESMEPM). At a minimum, we would like to change the specialization name so that “Environmental Policy and Management” will appear on transcripts even if the ecampus code remains the same. 6.
